title: What If You Could Read Your Crush's MIND?
description:
Dr. Osei is about to drive ninety minutes on the motorway after twenty hours awake, and only Glint knows, because he heard Dr. Osei think it. On the museum's Late Night, a cracked helium pipe on an old brain-scanner helmet leaves Glint hearing the thoughts of everyone whose voice he has listened to for hours: Nan, Kai, Dr. Osei, and Maya, the planetarium volunteer he has liked for a whole year. Nobody believes how he knows. So Glint turns the real trick people use to beat brain decoders (counting backwards by sevens) into a test. And Maya has a secret of her own.

The rules are real science: the 2023 UT Austin decoder that turned brain scans into gist sentences, MEG brain decoding, inner speech, the cocktail party effect, and what being awake too long does to a driver.

If you could read your crush's mind, would you want to? And would you let them read yours? Tell me in the comments 👇

CHAPTERS
0:00 Cold open: twenty hours awake
0:26 Late Night: the Mind Readers helmet
1:27 The Rules: gist, not words
2:39 Plus: Maya
3:21 Plus: Nan's inner voice
3:47 Plus: Kai thinks in pictures
4:05 Minus: The noise
4:43 Minus: What Kai really thinks
5:11 Minus: Dr. Osei
5:28 The Crisis: fifteen minutes
6:55 The Solution: count backwards by sevens
8:10 The Twist: she heard everything
8:56 Would you?

SOURCES
• Tang, LeBel, Jain & Huth, Nature Neuroscience 26: 858–866 (2023): semantic decoder from fMRI, about 16 hours of training per person, gist not exact words, needs cooperation, beaten by counting by sevens
• Défossez et al., Nature Machine Intelligence 5 (2023); Benchetrit, Banville & King (ICLR 2024): decoding speech and images from MEG
• Alderson-Day & Fernyhough, Psychological Bulletin 141 (2015); Vygotsky, Thought and Language (1934): inner speech is condensed
• Heavey & Hurlburt, Consciousness and Cognition 17 (2008): inner speech in about a quarter of sampled moments
• Nedergaard & Lupyan, Psychological Science (2024): some people have little or no inner voice
• Cherry, JASA 25 (1953); Moray (1959); Wood & Cowan (1995): the cocktail party effect and hearing your own name
• Dawson & Reid, Nature 388 (1997); Williamson & Feyer, Occup. Environ. Med. 57 (2000): sleep loss impairs like alcohol
• Boyle et al., Transportation Research F 11 (2008): microsleeps while driving
• Reyner & Horne, Sleep 21 (1998): cold air and radio barely help sleepy drivers
• NASA Saturn fact sheet: Saturn is less dense than water
• Story is fiction: Glint's power, Maya's power and every heard thought are made up; the science rules are real.
